tasks.short: Assess suspected violations and report them to the appropriate authority.

steps.what: Assemble incident records and supporting evidence from the {DOCS}.
Compare evidence with applicable obligations and record possible breaches.

loop.input: Evidence bundle and approved, versioned obligations for the relevant jurisdiction.
loop.output: Possible breaches, contrary evidence, uncertainties and source references.
loop.check: Require valid source references; the officer checks applicability and factual support.
loop.stop: One assessment and one correction pass; unresolved questions return to the officer.
loop.why_not_simpler: Narrative evidence and contextual obligations cannot all be compared through fixed fields.

steps.what: Decide reporting duty, recipient, deadline and information scope.
Draft the violation report and identify its supporting attachments.

loop.input: Reporting decision, approved template and referenced evidence.
loop.output: Draft report with evidence references and explicit missing information.
loop.check: Validate required fields and references; the officer checks claims and disclosure scope.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; unsupported statements remain flagged for manual completion.
loop.why_not_simpler: The factual narrative varies by incident; fixed fields alone cannot express it.

steps.what: Review the report and authorise its disclosure.
Submit the approved report through the {GOV_PORTAL}.
File the submission receipt and update the case status in the {WORKFLOW}.

tasks.design: A case flow in the {WORKFLOW} retrieves authorised evidence from the {DOCS}, checks deadlines and runs bounded assessment and drafting loops. The officer decides reportability, and an authorised signatory approves the exact disclosure before a deterministic connector submits it through the {GOV_PORTAL} and records the receipt.
tasks.previous_blocker: Evidence is scattered, obligations require interpretation, and submission channels differ. Templates alone do not assemble a defensible report.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing case flows and document access can support deterministic collection and deadline checks. Bounded drafting can reduce narrative work when every claim retains its source.
tasks.still_hard: Reporting thresholds, privilege, conflicting obligations and urgent deadlines remain difficult. Some authorities offer no supported submission interface.
tasks.human_edge: Recognising material facts, resolving legal ambiguity and accepting responsibility for disclosure.

ambition.what: Daily prioritisation of incidents approaching a reporting deadline.

tasks.altitude: The officer spends less time assembling and filing reports and more time assessing evidence and urgent cases. Legal reporting and disclosure authority remain with the existing authorised roles.

reach.task: Prepare a traceable evidence pack for a control failure.
reach.learn: Evidence provenance, control testing and reconciliation to source records.

reach.task: Prioritise incidents by potential financial exposure.
reach.learn: Exposure estimation, uncertainty ranges and escalation thresholds.

evidence.claim: Case assembly, deadline checks and receipt logging can use deterministic workflows; these are design estimates.
Veeva RIM tracks registrations and publishes submissions in a specialised regulatory setting; this is adjacent capability evidence.
The documented flawed-report case supports checking generated claims against their original sources.

assumptions: The company has a compliance function and reports violations relevant to its activities.
Step shares are illustrative, not measured. Evidence assessment and approval remain substantial despite the workflow-automation prior.
Automatic submission requires a supported interface and an approval bound to the exact report, attachments and recipient.
Build ranges cover one reporting route and are working-day estimates, not elapsed delivery promises.
GDPR applies to personal evidence; EU AI Act applicability depends on intended use. Access work includes national consultation requirements where applicable.
unknowns: Applicable reporting regimes, recipients and deadlines.
Who may approve disclosure and whether urgent cases have a delegated route.
Supported submission interfaces and authentication methods.
Evidence sensitivity, retention periods and privilege restrictions.
Whether employee-data processing triggers consultation under national rules.
research_questions: Which reporting routes support reliable submission acknowledgements and duplicate prevention?
Which report sections can use fixed fields without a drafting loop?
new_work: Review cited assessments and generated report narratives.
Maintain obligation versions, recipient mappings and deadline rules.
Handle unavailable submission channels and uncertain delivery.
Audit approval records, access permissions and disclosure scope.

tasks.short: Interview applicants and specialists to clarify facts relevant to licensing decisions.

steps.what: Read the application file and prepare questions about missing or conflicting facts.

loop.input: Application file and approved licensing standards.
loop.output: Source-linked evidence gaps, contradictions and suggested neutral questions.
loop.check: Validate source references; the officer checks relevance and removes unsupported assumptions.
loop.stop: One brief and one correction pass; unresolved gaps remain questions for the interview.
loop.why_not_simpler: Narrative applications can contain inconsistencies that required-field checks cannot identify.

steps.what: Arrange the interview and request outstanding documents through the {EMAIL}.
Interview the applicant or specialist and probe relevant uncertainties.
Write a factual interview summary and list unresolved questions.

loop.input: Officer's interview notes and supplied evidence.
loop.output: Attributed factual summary separating statements, documents and unresolved questions.
loop.check: The officer verifies attribution, omissions and references against the original notes.
loop.stop: One summary and one revision; ambiguous passages return to manual editing.
loop.why_not_simpler: Free-text notes require synthesis; fixed forms cannot reliably preserve their meaning.

steps.what: Clarify disputed technical facts through the {EMAIL}.
Attach the reviewed summary and clarification to the application file.

tasks.design: A case flow in the {WORKFLOW} prepares a source-linked interview brief from the {DOCS} and arranges appointments through the {EMAIL} and {CALENDAR}. The officer conducts the interview, reviews a bounded summary drafted from their notes, and files the reviewed record for the licensing decision.
tasks.previous_blocker: The main work is a contextual conversation. Preparation and note writing depend on varied application documents that simple scheduling tools cannot interpret.
tasks.enabler_now: Scheduling and filing can use existing configuration. Small document-reading and drafting loops can prepare questions and summaries without replacing the interview.
tasks.still_hard: Building trust, probing evasive answers, accommodating communication needs and resolving specialist disagreement.
tasks.human_edge: Asking fair follow-up questions and understanding explanations in context without treating demeanour as proof.

ambition.what: An applicant-facing evidence-gap checklist before the interview.

tasks.altitude: The officer spends more of the week on substantive interviews and difficult factual questions. No licensing decision rights change.

reach.task: Prepare a neutral chronology for a fact-finding interview.
reach.learn: Non-leading questions, evidence attribution and separating inconsistency from deception.

reach.task: Request specialist evidence needed to resolve an eligibility question.
reach.learn: Scope precise evidence requests and document the limits of specialist conclusions.

evidence.claim: Scheduling, document requests and filing can be configured; interview preparation and summaries can use bounded model loops.
Workplace emotion recognition is prohibited under the EU AI Act; it is excluded from this design.

assumptions: Licensing interviews apply only where the company operates an authorised licensing or certification service.
Step shares are illustrative. Conversation remains the largest share, consistent with the supplied means prior.
The design uses officer-written notes and introduces no recording, emotion analysis or applicant scoring.
Scheduling messages use approved templates and minimum necessary case details.
The evidence-gap checklist requires officer review before applicant delivery.
GDPR applies to application records. Access estimates include national consultation requirements where applicable.
unknowns: Whether this licensing activity exists in the company.
Interview participants, languages and accessibility needs.
Which documents may be shared with external specialists.
Required opportunities for applicants to correct factual records.
Case volumes, interview duration and retention requirements.
research_questions: Which common evidence gaps can be detected using form validation alone?
What summary format best preserves attribution and unresolved disagreement?
new_work: Review suggested questions and applicant-facing evidence requests.
Check summaries for omissions, attribution errors and unsupported conclusions.
Maintain interview templates and document-access rules.
Handle scheduling exceptions and accessible participation requests.

tasks.short: Review eligibility and issue licences within an authorised licensing mandate.

steps.what: Register the application in the {OTHER} licensing register.
Check qualifications and supporting documents against the application.

loop.input: Application documents and required evidence fields.
loop.output: Evidence fields with page references, missing items and conflicting details.
loop.check: Validate field formats and dates; the officer verifies material facts and authenticity separately.
loop.stop: One extraction and one retry for failed fields; uncertain items enter manual review.
loop.why_not_simpler: Supporting documents vary in layout and wording; structured submissions bypass the loop.

steps.what: Complete the standards checklist, including payment status where required.
Decide eligibility, conditions and permitted validity period.
Prepare the licence certificate from the approved decision.
Send the authorised licence certificate to the applicant through the {EMAIL}.
Record licence status and expiry in the {OTHER} licensing register.

tasks.design: Configure the {OTHER} licensing register for structured intake and completeness checks, with a bounded extraction loop for documents in the {DOCS}. Deterministic rules prepare the eligibility checklist; the licensing officer authorises the decision, after which a generator creates the certificate and the {WORKFLOW} sends it through the {EMAIL} and updates the register.
tasks.previous_blocker: Evidence arrives in varied documents, standards contain discretionary elements, and certificate preparation is separated from the eligibility record.
tasks.enabler_now: Structured intake, versioned rules and template generation already support much of the work. Bounded extraction can handle document variation without making the licensing decision.
tasks.still_hard: Authenticity checks, recognition of equivalent qualifications, discretionary conditions and appeals. Integration cannot create a legal power to issue licences.
tasks.human_edge: Applying standards fairly to unusual evidence and giving a defensible reason for conditions or refusal.
tasks.altitude: The officer reviews eligibility and exceptional evidence instead of rekeying documents and producing certificates. Statutory powers and delegated decision rights remain unchanged.

reach.task: Assess whether evidence satisfies a defined authorisation requirement.
reach.learn: Evidence sufficiency, qualification equivalence and reasoned decision records.

reach.task: Analyse application delays by evidence gap and review stage.
reach.learn: Event definitions, cohort analysis and avoiding misleading averages.

evidence.claim: Structured intake, versioned eligibility rules and certificate templates can automate administration while retaining human decisions.
Veeva RIM supports registration records and regulatory submissions; it does not establish this individual-licensing use case.
GDPR Article 22 restricts solely automated decisions with legal or similarly significant effects, subject to its exceptions and safeguards.

assumptions: Most mid-size companies apply for licences rather than issue them. This task applies only to an authorised issuer or delegated operator.
The scenario covers one licence family and an existing licensing register that supports configuration.
Step shares are illustrative. Clear rule coverage supports automated checks, but those checks are not the final decision.
The updated application file includes any required interview record; a complete initial file can serve the same purpose.
Issuance authorisation specifies identity, licence type, conditions and validity. Generated certificates must match it exactly before release.
GDPR and the EU AI Act apply as relevant; national rules determine licensing powers, procedure and consultation requirements.
unknowns: Whether the company has any licence-issuing mandate.
Which standards are objective and which require discretion.
Required identity, authenticity and qualification checks.
Signature, certificate-format and delivery requirements.
Payment prerequisites, appeal rights and publication obligations.
Existing register interfaces and employee consultation requirements.
research_questions: Which licence fields and checks can be configured in the existing register?
Which decisions require a legally designated officer or an additional signatory?
How will the release process prevent duplicate or unauthorised certificates?
new_work: Verify extracted evidence and investigate authenticity concerns.
Maintain versioned standards, fee prerequisites and certificate templates.
Test changes against borderline and historical cases.
Handle delivery failures, corrections, revocations and appeals.
Review access logs and decision traceability.

tasks.short: Assess licence fees, collect payments and resolve payment exceptions.

steps.what: Determine the licence fee and any applicable exemption in the {ERP}.
Issue the fee invoice and payment instructions from the {ERP}.
Match imported {BANK} transactions to fee invoices in the {ERP}.
Investigate unmatched payments and disputed fees through the {EMAIL}.
Approve fee adjustments or refunds within delegated limits in the {ERP}.
Send payment reminders through the {EMAIL} for undisputed overdue invoices.
Update payment status in the {OTHER} licensing register.

tasks.design: Configure the {ERP} to calculate published fees, issue invoices with unique references and send scheduled reminders through the {EMAIL}. A deterministic connector matches imported {BANK} transactions and synchronises payment status with the {OTHER} licensing register; staff investigate exceptions and a finance manager approves adjustments.
tasks.previous_blocker: Payment references and application identifiers do not consistently align across the licensing register and the {ERP}. Responsibility crosses licensing and finance teams.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing invoicing and reconciliation features can handle routine cases once identifiers and fee rules are aligned. A small connector can replace repeated payment-status checks.
tasks.still_hard: Third-party payers, partial payments, disputed exemptions and refunds. Fee changes and settlement timing must remain consistent across records.
tasks.human_edge: Resolving disputed charges fairly and distinguishing payment mistakes from genuine entitlement to an adjustment.
tasks.altitude: The officer stops checking routine receipts and works mainly on disputed fees and licensing prerequisites. Finance retains adjustment and payment authority; no new decision rights are assumed.

reach.task: Maintain accurate invoice references and fee categories.
reach.learn: Receivables controls, exemption evidence and invoice correction procedures.

reach.task: Reconcile licence receipts to open invoices.
reach.learn: Partial-payment handling, duplicate detection and settlement reconciliation.

evidence.claim: Published fee rules, invoicing, reference matching and reminders are primarily deterministic finance operations.
Transporeon checks freight invoices against agreed rates; this supports the narrower principle of rule-based amount checking, not licence-fee collection.

assumptions: This task applies only where the company legitimately charges licence or certification fees.
Published fees and standard exemptions can be represented as approved rules.
The {ERP} supports invoicing, imported bank transactions and approval configuration.
Step shares are illustrative. The structured payment steps support more automation than the supplied human-task prior suggests.
Ambiguous matches remain unmatched; the design uses no model loop and makes no automatic withdrawal from applicants.
Refund execution remains in the existing treasury process after approval; it is outside this fee-collection task.
GDPR applies to payer data. Access estimates include segregation of duties and any consultation required under national rules.
unknowns: Whether licence fees are charged and who legally sets them.
Fee schedules, tax treatment and exemption rules.
Payment channels, reference quality and reconciliation volumes.
Bank-feed availability and register integration support.
Refund authority, approval limits and existing treasury controls.
research_questions: Can existing {ERP} matching rules resolve routine receipts without custom matching code?
Which settlement events are sufficient to mark an application paid?
How should disputed invoices suppress reminders across both records?
new_work: Maintain fee schedules, exemption rules and application-reference mappings.
Investigate unmatched, duplicate and partial payments.
Monitor import failures and reconciliation totals.
Review adjustment requests and route approved refunds to treasury.
Check that disputed or paid invoices do not receive reminders.

role.altitude: The compliance officer spends more time interpreting obligations, conducting interviews and resolving contested evidence. Preparation, record updates and routine fee administration shrink, while existing legal and financial approval rights remain explicit.
reach: Accountants and auditors: prepare traceable evidence packs and test control failures.
Financial risk specialists: prioritise incidents using exposure and reporting deadlines.
Financial examiners: assess evidence sufficiency for authorisation decisions.
Billing and posting clerks: maintain reliable fee and payment records.
skills_to_grow: Translate obligations into versioned checks with explicit exceptions.
Verify source-linked model outputs and identify unsupported conclusions.
Conduct fair interviews and preserve evidence attribution.
Understand record identifiers, reconciliation and approval controls.
Assess GDPR and EU AI Act applicability and relevant national rules.
role.ambitious_version: A compliance evidence service that gives applicants and internal teams early completeness checks, while officers focus on difficult facts, defensible decisions and timely regulatory reporting.
